t: In nineteen eighty-four, a young doctor in Australia drank a glass of bacteria. On purpose.
His name was Barry Marshall, and almost nobody believed him.
Back then, doctors were sure stomach ulcers came from stress and spicy food. Some patients even had part of their stomach removed.
Marshall and his colleague Robin Warren blamed a tiny spiral bacterium.
The experts laughed. So he made himself the experiment.
Three days later, he was throwing up, and his mom said his breath was awful.
A camera in his stomach showed it: inflamed, and full of the bacteria.
A few antibiotics, and he was fine.
Today, most ulcers are cured in about two weeks. And in two thousand five, Marshall and Warren won the Nobel Prize.
Would you drink it to prove you're right? Tell me in the comments.
